title: Proof-of-concept scans of known structures
place_text: Gran Sasso Laboratory, Italy; Osiris Shaft, Egypt

tellings.quote: And this technology was very good at accurately detecting the known structures within these modern facilities that were scanned. But also the Osiris shaft, too.

plain: Before it was used on Egypt's pyramids, a scanning method was tested on structures whose layout was already known, according to a researcher named Jeffrey Drum. One test site was the Gran Sasso Laboratory, a modern facility in Italy. Another was the Osiris Shaft, a known shaft in Egypt. Drum tells Michels the method, which he credits to a researcher named Filippo Biondi, was "very good at accurately detecting the known structures within these modern facilities," and the Osiris Shaft as well. The point of the tests is that a method which finds known structures correctly gives more weight to what it reports beneath the pyramids.
